title: Alberta man's death in Leduc prompts anti-Taser petition
article: An online petition calling for tighter restrictions on stun gun use has been launched after a man died after he was zapped by a Taser in Leduc by Mounties last weekend.
A petition entitled " Canadian Police: Don't Tase First, Ask Questions Later !" surfaced on ThePetitionSite.com on Aug. 5 and so far has more than 1,800 of 5,000 requested signatures.
"It's time for all provinces to start taking Taser safety seriously," says the petition started by "Susan V" targeting the Alberta RCMP.
The petition was made in response to the death of a 27-year-old man who was in a physical altercation with Leduc RCMP at a gas station at 50 Street and 50 Avenue in Leduc on Aug. 2.
Mounties were responding to multiple calls of assaults, car thefts and hit-and-run collisions in relation to the incident, which ended in the man's arrest after police deployed a Taser.
The man was placed under arrest and was in custody when police realized the man was in "medical distress," according to an RCMP release.
Emergency services responded, and the suspect was brought to Leduc Hospital before being transferred to the Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton where he died Aug. 4.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team is still investigating.
"There is no correlation between the use of the Taser and the reason why the man was taken to hospital," said ASIRT spokeswoman Sarah Jackson last weekend.
"That will come out in the investigation."
The man was identified in a CTV Edmonton report as Marc-Andre Fontaine, a father of three young children.

Several noted deaths after police Taser use have been caused by excited delirium due to multiple drug toxicity. Victims typically display aggressive behaviour and can take several people to restrain them.
New rules around police Taser use were introduced in Canada in 2010 after the infamous airport death of Polish immigrant Robert Dziekanski.
Officers are required to only use stun guns when a subject is causing bodily harm or when the officer believes harm is imminent.
They have to give a verbal warning and are ordered not to stun a person multiple times or use the weapon for more than five seconds.
